topics.topic: How to reference the connections-file encoding and byte-order-mark policy through an imported provider constant
questions: Replace the inline encoding and byte-order-mark policy with the name of an imported provider constant that carries that policy.
The encoding and byte-order-mark policy must be placed in a provider constant and named as `the imported X constant`, with that symbol added to the module's imports.

quotes: _connections_file: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST return content validated strictly against = models.ConnectionsFile only when it is one JSON text in UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, in which no object repeats a member name, whose only member is objects, each key of objects the canonical lowercase hyphenated spelling of a UUID, and each value a ConnectionEntry with exactly its fields, each of its declared type without coercion; it MUST raise ValueError for any other content.
judgement.why: The note spells out a policy value that generated code must read instead of naming it through the required imported provider constant form.
judgement.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.

topics.topic: How to specify the forbidden parent-directory segment in the subfolder rule
questions: Replace the literal path micro-syntax with a semantic requirement such as forbidding parent-directory segments.

quotes: _subfolder: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST return the value unchanged only when it is a string holding a non-empty relative path none of whose segments is .. and which does not name the root itself, and MUST raise ValueError for any other value.

topics.topic: Whether and how to replace literal port-range bounds with a provider-owned imported policy constant
questions: Replace the inline bounds 1 and 65535 with a reference to an imported policy constant, adding that constant to IMPORTS and the imported data-access signatures, or restore the semantic condition that the port is one TCP cannot address.
The literal port-range thresholds 1 and 65535 must be moved to a provider-owned imported constant, and the note must name that imported constant instead of embedding the values.
Must the literal port bounds be replaced by an imported policy constant added to IMPORTS, or must the requirement stop specifying those values?
The note must replace the inline threshold `1 to 65535` with the name of an imported constant that supplies the port-range policy.
